summary: Describes how OSPF operates over ATM networks using permanent and switched virtual circuits, in the presence of Proxy-PAR. It is an experimental protocol.

eli5.summary: This explains how a router-to-router chat can run over an older kind of network built on pre-arranged connections, and use a helper to find neighbors.

subtitle: Running OSPF routing over ATM networks using virtual circuits and auto-discovery

tldr.problem: OSPF assumes either broadcast networks (like Ethernet) or point-to-point links, but ATM networks are non-broadcast (no broadcast capability but can have many routers on the same subnet). Standard OSPF NBMA mode requires manual configuration of all neighbors.
tldr.mechanism: This RFC specifies how OSPF operates as virtual interfaces over ATM, modeling collections of virtual circuits (VCs) as NBMA or point-to-multipoint logical interfaces. It describes how Proxy-PAR (an ATM protocol for registering and discovering services) can automatically populate neighbor lists, avoiding manual configuration.
tldr.outcome: OSPF routers on ATM networks can discover each other and manage large VC meshes dynamically, reducing manual configuration and allowing more flexible network designs. Logical interfaces decouple IP addressing and VC management, enabling simpler large-scale ATM deployments.

today: RFC 2844 is an Experimental protocol and has not been updated or obsoleted. OSPF over ATM never achieved widespread deployment; most operators and enterprises moved away from ATM toward Ethernet and MPLS for core networks. Proxy-PAR, while standardized by the ATM Forum, saw limited adoption outside specialized carrier environments. Modern deployments use Ethernet, MPLS, or pure IP-based discovery mechanisms rather than OSPF over ATM with Proxy-PAR.

sections.title: The Challenge of OSPF Over ATM
sections.content:
OSPF (Open Shortest Path First) is an Interior Gateway Protocol designed for link-state routing. It works well over broadcast networks (like Ethernet, where one message reaches all routers) and point-to-point links (where exactly two routers are connected). However, ATM networks present a different model: no broadcast capability, but multiple routers can be logically attached to the same IP subnet through a set of pre-configured virtual circuits.

Standard OSPF supports non-broadcast multi-access (NBMA) networks, but requires that the list of neighbors be manually configured on each router. For large ATM deployments, this becomes a configuration nightmare. In addition, ATM networks typically have pre-arranged virtual circuit (VC) meshes, where the topology is not dynamic (unlike newer SVC-capable networks with on-demand circuit setup).

This RFC describes how to use Proxy-PAR (an ATM service registration and discovery mechanism) to automate the discovery of OSPF neighbors on ATM networks. It also specifies how OSPF virtual interfaces can be modeled as logical interfaces, each consisting of one or more VCs, configured as point-to-point, NBMA, or point-to-multipoint interfaces.
sections.eli5: ATM is like a party line phone system where you call people one at a time. Routers need to know who else is on the line. A helper (Proxy-PAR) can tell each router who the others are, so they do not need a manual list.

sections.title: Virtual Interfaces and Logical Models
sections.content:
The core concept is the logical interface. A logical interface represents a subnet and consists of one or more virtual circuits. It is configured with a type (point-to-point, NBMA, or point-to-multipoint), an IP address, a subnet mask, a VPN ID (virtual private network), and layer 2 parameters (address resolution method, QoS class, etc.).

A single physical ATM interface on a router may carry multiple logical interfaces, each with its own IP subnet and VPN. Each logical interface maintains its own OSPF neighbor relationships and can operate independently. This decoupling allows routers to support complex multi-subnet, multi-VPN topologies over shared ATM infrastructure.

For an NBMA logical interface, one or more VCs connect the local router to each neighboring router. For point-to-multipoint, a set of VCs to different neighbors is present, but they are not assumed to form a fully-meshed topology. For point-to-point, a single VC connects two routers. The VC or set of VCs is the Layer 2 substrate; OSPF operates at Layer 3 and is unaware of the VC structure.
sections.eli5: An IP network is drawn on top of ATM pipes. Several networks can share the same physical ATM port if they are separated by VPN numbers. Each network can use one big mesh, a partial mesh, or just point-to-point links, and OSPF adapts to the shape.

sections.title: Proxy-PAR Auto-Discovery and Configuration
sections.content:
Proxy-PAR is an ATM Forum standard that allows non-ATM devices (like routers) to register services with the ATM network and to query for services registered by other devices. Each registration includes information such as the service type, address, and VPN scope. Registrations are flooded by the ATM switch fabric only within the specified scope (a PNNI routing level), which bounds scalability.

For NBMA interfaces, a router queries Proxy-PAR with its own IP subnet and VPN ID to discover all other OSPF routers on the same subnet. Each router registers its OSPF parameters: the IP address, subnet mask, area ID, interface type, and priority. On receiving a query result, a router can populate its neighbor list with the addresses and priorities of discovered neighbors. It then initiates VCs to each neighbor as required by OSPF.

For point-to-multipoint interfaces, the discovery process is similar, but the router installs as neighbors only those routers for which it already has a VC (from prior PVC setup) and whose address it can resolve. For point-to-point interfaces, the router can register itself and discover a unique peer through Proxy-PAR rather than relying on multicast Hello discovery.

Proxy-PAR provides a key advantage over manual configuration: neighbor lists are dynamic and respond to changes in the ATM network topology. As routers are added or removed, they register or deregister, and existing routers learn of these changes through subsequent Proxy-PAR queries.
sections.eli5: When a router starts, it posts to the ATM network 'I am an OSPF router on subnet 10.0.0.0'. Other routers see the posting and know to call it. If a router shuts down, it stops posting and others stop calling it.

sections.title: IP Address to ATM Address Resolution
sections.content:
The mapping between IP addresses and ATM addresses (NSAPs) is a long-standing challenge in ATM networking. Traditional approaches include ATMARP and Classical IP over ATM. This RFC describes how Proxy-PAR registrations can serve as a source for IP-to-NSAP resolution without requiring a separate ARP server.

When a router registers an OSPF interface with Proxy-PAR, it provides the IP address, subnet mask, and its ATM address (NSAP). Other routers that query the same subnet learn both the IP addresses and the corresponding NSAPs of all neighbors. This information can be cached in an IP-to-NSAP resolution table, allowing the router's data-forwarding component to resolve the destination IP address of a data packet directly to an ATM address without separate ARP messages.

This approach simplifies the set of protocols required to operate OSPF over ATM: a single registration and query mechanism (Proxy-PAR) serves both neighbor discovery and address resolution functions.
sections.eli5: When routers tell the ATM network about themselves, they include both their IP address and their ATM phone number. Other routers learn both at the same time and can connect calls without asking extra questions.

sections.title: Establishing Connections in PVC and SVC Environments
sections.content:
Two deployment scenarios are described: permanent virtual circuits (PVCs) and switched virtual circuits (SVCs).

In PVC environments, the VC mesh is manually configured in advance and does not change. OSPF discovers neighbors through Proxy-PAR, but the underlying VCs are static. A router can only establish OSPF adjacencies with neighbors for which a VC is already present. Dynamic configuration of the VC mesh is not possible, but this simplifies the deployment: administrators pre-build the mesh and OSPF learns the topology through discovery.

In SVC environments, VCs can be established dynamically as needed. When OSPF discovers a new neighbor through Proxy-PAR and determines that an OSPF Hello must be sent, the router can initiate an SVC to that neighbor on-demand. However, this introduces a race condition: both ends might initiate an SVC simultaneously. The RFC specifies that the router with the lower IP address on the interface should detect the peer's VC and close its own, reusing the peer's connection. This behavior is coordinated with OSPF Demand Circuits extensions (RFC 1793) to allow graceful teardown of unused VCs.
sections.eli5: If ATM pipes are set up in advance, OSPF just uses them. If routers can set up pipes on the fly, they race to dial each other, and the loser hangs up and uses the winner's call.

sections.title: Security and Access Control
sections.content:
The RFC notes that security of OSPF over ATM depends on multiple layers. At the ATM layer, the PNNI protocol provides some security for registered information, but Proxy-PAR registrations themselves are not authenticated. An attacker with access to the ATM network could register false service entries or intercept Proxy-PAR queries, leading to misrouting or denial of service.

The solution relies on OSPF's own security mechanisms. OSPF can use authentication (password or cryptographic) on OSPF messages to verify that Hello messages and topology updates come from authorized routers. Even if Proxy-PAR registrations are spoofed, OSPF authentication prevents an attacker from forging adjacencies or fake routing information.

Administrators must carefully manage access to Proxy-PAR registration and query mechanisms, just as they would manage access to SNMP MIBs or configuration interfaces. The decoupling of layer 2 (ATM) and layer 3 (OSPF) topology means that an attacker must compromise both to achieve effective attacks.
sections.eli5: The ATM helper is not very secure, so OSPF adds password checking. Even if an attacker tricks the helper, the password keeps them out.
